sampling_model.design: For each common \(\rho\in I\), independently across the fixed finite nonempty set \(S\), draw a simple-random stage-1 holdout and a balanced complete-randomization assignment. Recompute every stratum selector, form the complete signed cell, and then generate independent balanced stage-2 assignments only in recruited strata conditional on the first-stage history. The Fisher reference rerandomizes the joint holdout--assignment action, recomputes the full cell, restricts to the observed cell, and only then generates stage 2.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite-population baseline triangular array indexed by two stages and an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set; the only randomness is the holdout and chronological assignment.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment is completely randomized with prespecified quotas in every stage-1 stratum and, after selection, in every recruited stage-2 stratum.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive limiting block shares, positive baseline and midrank variance margins, fixed positive sampling- and reference-cell probability margins, and \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\) keep all divisions, conditioning operations, and Gaussian quantiles nondegenerate.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proof controls hypergeometric complement counts, complement and rank studentizers, local rank crossings, mean--rank covariances, the Fisher-completed reference array, and moving critical values. Maximum influence is derived from the fourth-moment, variance, and positive-share primitives rather than assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For the present design, augmenting the first action to the joint holdout--assignment pair makes the same-selection conditional reference in Proposition 2 exactly the explicit Fisher kernel, and Proposition 1 gives the same conditional validity conclusion; their broader multistage class does not provide the Gaussian holdout--power frontier.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 2 provide the multivariate complete-randomization Gaussian substrate used after the present maximum-influence and random-complement reductions.
Theorem 1 provides Gaussian approximation ingredients for linear permutation contrasts, but not the present selected, studentized, random-complement reference transfer.
Theorem 9 supplies an independent-sampling randomized-selection transfer architecture, whereas the present theorem treats without-replacement randomization and an imputed Fisher reference.
Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 supply the Gaussian convexity and equality theorem from which the selected-quantile result is derived.

Their normal model-based two-stage policy architecture is nonnested with the present exact design-based problem and optimizes an expected-sample-size and familywise-error objective, so none of their optimality conclusions transfers to the conditional local-power frontier.
Their Gaussian location-model conditional-inference result concerns leftover information in a parametric adaptive experiment, not fixed finite-population selective randomization power.

body.tldr: For an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set \(S\) and two stages, each common holdout fraction \(\rho\) defines a chronological finite-population randomization law and a same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. Treating the randomized pair \((H,Z_1)\) as the first augmented action gives an exact Freidling--Zhao--Gao representation: recomputation on the full signed cell yields their computable conditional reference, while the finite-support tail argument gives exact selective level. A per-array common remainder transfers the shifted sampling law and the data-dependent zero-drift reference law, including random complement counts, studentization, rank stability, and quantiles. The resulting Gaussian criterion reduces arbitrary compact positive alternatives to their least coordinates; \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) determines the weight side, nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, the explicit two-stratum mixture supplies a certified interior counterexample, and the complete mixed-sign optimizer is characterized by equality-aware analytic branches and tolerance-certified boxes.

project_justification.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao provide a broad multistage validity and computability representation, but not a finite-population Gaussian local-power frontier or an optimal holdout rule. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, randomized-selection transfer results use independent sampling, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu study a nonnested normal model-based policy problem with expected-sample-size and familywise-error criteria. None supplies the present full-signed-cell, random-complement, studentized transfer and maximin optimizer.
project_justification.niche: The missing design object is the common scalar holdout fraction and finite vector of cell-specific nonnegative unit-norm stage weights for an arbitrary fixed finite stratum set. Selection changes both the conditional law and retained stage-1 information, so the optimizer can be an endpoint, an interior point, or a set-valued mixed-sign branch correspondence.
project_justification.fill: The note embeds the joint holdout--assignment pair as the randomized first action, enumerates its exact same-cell Fisher support, proves sharp-zero conditional validity, and derives one per-array uniform transfer to shifted sampling and zero-drift reference Gaussian laws. Finite-product cancellation reduces each active pair to a scalar selected integral. Ehrhard convexity, inverse-Mills differentiation, a finite-population realizability inequality, an explicit two-stratum negative-discrepancy witness, semianalytic branch exhaustion, and interval boxes then give the claimed frontier without an exact-real equality oracle.

body.related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Propositions 1 and 2 are formally specialized by augmenting the first randomized action to \((H,Z_1)\): its known product law rerandomizes both the independent holdout and assignment, the selector is the complete label \(C\), and the stage-2 action depends on the past through that label. Sharp-zero imputability makes their reference computable, and the resulting restricted kernel is exactly the one enumerated here. Their broader multistage validity class supplies neither the Gaussian power limit nor the holdout--weight optimizer. Li and Ding supply the finite-population vector central limit theorem, while Shi and Ding supply quantitative permutation ingredients; the present transfer adds random complements, studentization, rank perturbations, signed-cell conditioning, and an imputed reference. Tian and Taylor provide a different independent-sampling selection-transfer architecture. Shenfeld and van Handel supply the Ehrhard--Borell theorem used to derive selected-quantile convexity. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu are a nonnested architectural comparator: their normal model-based policies optimize expected sample size subject to familywise-error and power constraints, not exact conditional-randomization local power, so no optimality result transfers. Chen and Andrews likewise study a parametric Gaussian adaptive experiment rather than this fixed-array design.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The transfer is per admissible baseline array: one deterministic remainder is uniform over its holdouts, weights, compact alternatives, and finitely many active cells, but no rate is uniform across the qualitative population class. Selection probabilities are bounded below by a fixed margin, so the result does not cover shrinking cells. The reference approximation is in the sampling probability associated with each design value, not under a simultaneous coupling of all holdouts. The two-stratum mixture is only an interior-optimum witness inside the arbitrary finite-stratum theory. The augmented-action proposition specializes Freidling--Zhao--Gao validity and computability only; all Gaussian and optimization conclusions require the separate finite-population transfer proved here.
body.honest_scope: Finite-sample exactness is limited to the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null. Positive alternatives are local constant effects on fixed potential-outcome arrays, and every design value has its own sampling law, dataset, completion, and reference kernel. The ambient stratum set is arbitrary but fixed, finite, and nonempty; the stage count remains two, the holdout fraction is common across strata, and \(J\) is finite. The scalar power formula applies only after complete signed-cell factor cancellation. The explicit negative mixture remains a two-stratum witness and does not establish uniqueness of its interior optimizer. General computation returns tolerance-certified value and optimizer-set boxes; a unique design is reported only with an explicit separation certificate. Binary outcomes, nonzero sharp-null inversion, weak average-effect nulls, shrinking selection margins, outcome-dependent deterministic splits, and continuous-biomarker cutoffs remain outside scope.
body.interpretation: The exact test remains valid for any fixed finite number of prespecified strata because the randomized action law and complete signed cell factor into finite products. The optimization is cellwise in the weights but coupled through the common holdout and worst-cell minimum. A nonnegative discrepancy certificate permits the closed-form largest holdout; a negative discrepancy can instead make an interior holdout strictly better, as the explicit two-stratum subcase proves. Mixed signs should therefore be reported as a certified value and optimizer correspondence unless a separation certificate isolates a unique design.
